title: The missing packers
subtitle: 01 / Move people, not the budget
brief: Two packers called out. Seven people are here, and orders keep arriving. You can move workers between stations, but nobody else can come in today.
goal: Complete at least 270 of 500 orders in at least 8 of 10 simulated shifts.
hint: Compare each station's processing time and worker count. Which station feeds work faster than the next can handle it?
lesson: The station with the longest task is not always the bottleneck. Staffing changes the rate. Once packing recovers, picking can become the next constraint.

title: People cannot fix everything
subtitle: 02 / Find the physical constraint
brief: Nine people showed up, but only one packing bench works. There is a spare bench available to rent for the shift. Decide whether moving people is enough.
goal: Complete at least 300 of 500 orders in at least 8 of 10 simulated shifts. Spend no more than $40 extra.
hint: How many people can actually pack at the same time? Extra workers cannot share a single occupied bench.
lesson: People and equipment are joint constraints. A worker assigned to a station is not necessarily a worker who can work.

title: The two-hour breakdown
subtitle: 03 / Buy the right recovery
brief: A packing failure will stop the whole station from minute 180 to 300. You have $60: rent one bench for $40, or pay $60 for a repair crew that cuts the stop to 30 minutes. A spare bench does not bypass this station-wide failure.
goal: Complete at least 420 of 650 orders in at least 8 of 10 simulated shifts. Spend no more than $60 extra.
hint: A bench adds capacity while the station is running. A repair changes how long it cannot run. Which loss are you trying to fix?
lesson: Capacity and availability solve different problems. Spend against the cause of the queue, not its most visible symptom.
